claim: Shah et al. 2003 define four ideation measures. Opened in full: novelty M1 = sum f_j S1_jk p_k with a posteriori S1 = (T-C)/T*10 (or an a priori expert scale of 3/7/10); variety M3 = sum f_j sum S_k b_k / n with genealogy-tree level weights 10/6/3/1 (physical principle, working principle, embodiment, detail), a one-branch level scoring zero; quality M2 scored against specs; quantity = raw count. Correlation a priori vs a posteriori novelty 0.944; each vs student peer ratings 0.59-0.62. The 2000 method-comparison numbers are still unread.
agent_test: Implement a posteriori novelty as (T-C)/T*10 per tagged attribute and variety as depth-weighted distinct-branch count; log both next to raw count; check on a known set whether adding a duplicate lowers novelty.

claim: Shah novelty metric is rarely used in original form (61 of 686 citing papers, about 9%) and inter-rater checks are rare; attribute and weight choices are mostly undocumented, so reported novelty numbers are weakly comparable.
agent_test: If we score novelty with an attribute scheme, fix attributes and weights before the run and report two-rater agreement.

claim: Frontier-LLM ideas are rated MORE novel than human ideas by blind expert reviewers in one-shot research ideation (5.64 and 5.81 vs 4.84 on a 1-10 scale, 79 reviewers; feasibility not different).
agent_test: Blind-rate agent ideas vs plain-model ideas at equal tokens with 3+ raters; do not trust one LLM judge.

claim: AI ideas lose their advantage after execution: scores drop 1.0 to 1.8 points more than human ideas (N=43 executed projects), and ideation scores barely predict execution scores (r from -0.32 to 0.21).
agent_test: Judge agent ideas by downstream test results, not by rated novelty alone; use execution-based reward where tasks allow.

claim: LLM output within one prompt is highly redundant: only about 5% of 4000 seed ideas are non-duplicates at cosine 0.8; same-prompt pair similarity above 0.8 is typical at temperature 1.0.
agent_test: Count distinct clusters per N samples at equal tokens for plain sampling vs scaffold; scaffold must raise cluster count.

claim: Cross-model homogeneity is real but its size is contested: Jiang reports cross-model similarity 0.71-0.82; Schaeffer shows a harder null (distinct ideas, same prompt) already gives 20-32% of pairs above 0.8, so the headline is inflated by embedding choice.
agent_test: Calibrate any diversity score against a known-distinct-ideas null before comparing arms.

claim: Human-only idea pools are more diverse than LLM pools (Terwiesch: gap B=0.193, 32 of 32 measures; Dong and Yakura: all simulated pools below all human pools). Newer models narrow but do not close the gap.
agent_test: Measure pool diversity (1 minus mean pairwise cosine) for N independent agent runs vs N plain samples.

claim: Prompting changes pool diversity a lot: chain-of-thought gave pairwise similarity 0.255 vs about 0.38 base (human 0.243); random personas 0.757 vs zero-shot 0.679 diversity; refine-twice agent was worse (0.575).
agent_test: Compare arms: base, CoT, persona/constraint injection, refine-loop at equal tokens; expect refine loops to hurt diversity.

claim: Iterative self-refinement of an LLM-made pool lowers diversity. Correction: the Terwiesch 'refine twice' arm ran on GPT-4o, so it is 0.575 vs GPT-4o zero-shot 0.679 (a 0.104 drop), not vs the older GPT-4 0.585. Uniform refinement of a pool raised the duplicate rate from 0.022 to 0.238 (Budgeted Subset Refinement). Refining a person's own seed ideas did not compress diversity (Dong and Yakura). Self-Refine below base on Claude (25/56 vs 30/56) is one more data point. Frontier-2026 models at equal tokens are still untested.
agent_test: Check whether our critique operator collapses diversity; log cluster count before and after each refine.

claim: Structured multi-path scaffolds raise path discovery (MUTATE: GPT-5.4 48.2% to 67.9%, Claude Sonnet 4.6 53.6% to 73.2%), method prompts raise top-5 novelty (IDEAFix), a two-step theme-then-write chain of thought raised unique category combinations from 39 to 55 (+42%, GPT-4o), and recoding-decoding gave 244 clusters from 250 ideas vs 35. All are single-group, none compares to best-of-N at equal tokens; diversity-forcing search (Heuresis, 3,222 runs) raised spread but not executed quality or novelty.
agent_test: Replicate on our own scenarios: forced-divergence operator vs plain at equal tokens.

claim: Human use of LLM ideas raises individual creativity ratings and fluency but lowers collective diversity (Doshi and Hauser: novelty +5.4%/+8.1%, similarity b=0.871/0.718; Anderson: ideas +15%, categories +27%; Dong and Yakura).
agent_test: Relevant only if humans use the agent; for the agent alone, test whether seeing its own prior ideas narrows later ones.

claim: The human homogenization effect is not reliably replicated: Wan and Kalman found no significant effect (N=97, p=.57, power 55%); Ashkinaze found global diversity UP with high AI exposure (Cliff's delta 0.31 disclosed, 0.26 undisclosed; ChatGPT-3.5, Alternative Uses, over 3,000 responses). Wan and Kalman 2025 also show diverse AI personas keep story diversity at baseline. Likely moderator: whether every person sees the same AI output (task, source variety, comparison arm).
agent_test: No agent test; treat human-effect size as unknown.

claim: Anderson group-level diversity gain is small and absent at individual level (0.24 vs 0.28, p=.038, d=.47; individual p=.352); uniqueness and flexibility measures show no difference. N=33 within-subject, comparison arm was Oblique Strategies cards, not no-aid.
agent_test: Metric choice flips conclusions; report at least three diversity measures.

claim: Design fixation can rise with generative AI and image search (Wadinambiarachchi N=60, human sketchers helped by Midjourney or image search: fixation .32 vs .27); this tests humans, not LLM fixation. For LLMs themselves, GPT-4o sessions fixate as much as humans across 10 sequential ideas (slope 1.013 vs 1.035, p=.51) and human seeds do not help, but no study I opened tests an LLM on a provided design exemplar. ChatGPT-assisted physical design placed second of six teams (14.8 m vs winner 37 m).
agent_test: Include a fixation probe: give the agent an example solution and test whether outputs copy its features.

claim: LLM judges are unreliable for novelty in zero-shot use: human reviewer agreement is only 56.1% yet LLM judges score 43-53%; one prompt sentence shifts pairwise accuracy by over 50 points; CreativityPrism finds novelty metrics correlating as low as -0.25. Expert panels themselves disagree on fine-grained scores (innovativeness alpha 0.33-0.47; coarse top-half Jaccard 0.43-0.71). With worked examples plus reasoning, a VLM judge reached expert-level agreement on uniqueness (expert-expert kappa 0.54) in a sketch study.
agent_test: Never let the agent self-score novelty as a selection signal; pair every LLM judge with a human or execution check.

claim: Embedding-based set metrics (cosine, centroid, convex hull) disagree with each other and depend on embedding model and length; hull volume of GPT-3 sets (0.186-0.266) is below crowd (0.294) while nearest-sample similarity is 0.75-0.80. On mechanism-level 'same idea' calls by 12 engineers, whole-text cosine reached only 0.51-0.56 accuracy (chance 0.5) against 0.871 for a structure graph; on coarse same/near/far cluster comparisons embeddings agreed with 30 experts in 10 of 12 cases. A style-neutralising rewrite kept 80-90% of the human-LLM diversity gap.
agent_test: Fix one embedding model and report 2-3 metrics; check correlation between metrics on our data.

claim: More agents or rounds give diminishing returns: three critic agents beat self-critique (non-duplicate 0.80 vs 0.77) and gains stop after about 3 agents, 8 rounds or a fourth turn.
agent_test: Sweep number of critique passes at equal tokens; stop where non-duplicate ratio stops rising.

claim: Prompt wording about creativity moves LLM variability only partly toward humans (population variability 0.459 baseline, 0.576 very creative with reward line vs human 0.738); single-answer originality matches humans (0.711 vs 0.696).
agent_test: Test whether a motivational line adds diversity beyond a structural operator.

claim: Persona diversity raises pool diversity in LLM-only runs (intra vs inter persona similarity 87.41 vs 82.93, d=1.43; random personas 0.757 vs 0.679) but did not reliably change human outputs.
agent_test: Persona-conditioned samples vs plain at equal tokens; measure cluster count.

claim: Ideation dimensions can move in opposite directions: LLM ideas had higher purchase intent (46-49% vs 40%) but lower novelty (36-37% vs 40.6%) and lower diversity; novelty vs intent r=-0.078.
agent_test: Report all four Shah dimensions per arm; do not collapse into one score.

claim: Within one session, GPT-4o shows the same fixation as humans over 10 ideas (categories 12.46 vs 12.68, p=.45), and the main LLM diversity loss is in the first idea of each session (categories 8.37 vs 14.51 per 10 first ideas). A non-embedding, category-based measure still shows the human advantage (22 vs 28 categories, 88 vs 206 combinations).
schema_part: S4 / operators that force a different first move
agent_test: Start each branch with a distinct framing (persona or constraint) chosen before generation, not after.

claim: Context-aware avoidance beats blind resampling: one GPT-4o session writing many ideas had diversity 0.679, independent one-idea sessions 0.452, the Bold-Ideas refine-twice arm 0.575; random personas 0.757, random constraints 0.735, chain of thought 0.698 (human 0.773).
agent_test: Prefer 'list what is already covered and generate outside it' to drawing N independent samples; compare against N independent samples at equal tokens.

claim: Diversity forcing alone does not convert to executed success: across 3,222 executed research-idea runs, MAP-Elites and Go-Explore were most diverse, no idea was rated 'Original', and only 1 of the top-10 by quality was also near-novel; the best novel idea trailed the best known recipe by 3.2% and 6.0% on two tasks.
agent_test: Do not use spread as the reward; log it as a diagnostic and verify ideas by execution or test.

claim: Refining all candidates is not the best use of tokens: refining 4 chosen candidates matched or beat refine-all (22.18 and 23.70 vs 21.80 strong non-duplicate ideas) at 105k vs 115k tokens, with the lowest duplicate rate (0.172) for the diversity-aware choice; raw generation and reranking gave 0.
schema_part: budget rule for critique and refine
agent_test: Select a small diverse subset for refinement (maximal marginal relevance) rather than critiquing everything.

claim: For plain LLM sampling, coverage of the human idea space keeps improving with N without plateau up to 1,000 (mean nearest distance 0.546 at N=100 to 0.478 at N=1,000; maximum 0.762 to 0.711), so the hardest human ideas stay hard to reach; the quality of the best idea rises with idea count, mean quality and variance (Girotra logic, restated).
agent_test: Treat more samples as slow, log-like returns; add a divergence operator before adding more samples.

claim: Human-LLM idea gaps are not only an embedding artefact: after neutralising style with an LLM rewrite 80% (zero-shot) to 90% (few-shot) of the diversity gap remained, and a category-based measure also shows it.
agent_test: Report any embedding diversity result alongside a style-neutralised or category-based check.

claim: Plain cosine on whole idea text cannot be trusted for the 'same idea' decision at the mechanism level (accuracy 0.51-0.56 vs chance 0.5), so thresholds like 0.8 should not be used alone; tagging purpose, mechanism and implementation first and comparing the tags came much closer to expert calls (0.871).
agent_test: Dedup on a tagged mechanism field, with cosine only as a pre-filter.
